articles.title: Cameron Underwood: Face transplant means I can smile again
articles.summary: The 26-year-old welder and machinist has had a face transplant after a failed suicide attempt in 2016.
articles.body:
Cameron Underwood says he doesn't get as many "stares or questions from strangers" since his face transplant.

"I have a nose, and a mouth so I'm able to smile, to speak and eat solid foods again," he says.

Cameron was speaking two years after shooting himself in a suicide attempt in 2016.

He lost his nose, most of his lower jaw and all but one of his teeth in the incident.

"I am so grateful to have a face transplant because it gives me a second chance at life," the 26-year-old said at a press conference in New York on Thursday.

"I have been able to get back to many of the activities I love, like being outdoors, playing sports and spending time with my friends and family.

"I hope to get back to work soon and someday to start a family."

In January this year, more than 100 medical staff performed a 25-hour surgery on Cameron at the NYU Langone Health centre in Manhattan, New York, and his recovery was revealed this week.

The operation took place just 18 months after Cameron's suicide attempt - which the centre says is the shortest period of time between injury and surgery in US history.

Since the first face transplant in 2005, more than 40 have been performed worldwide.

The surgery was led by Dr Eduardo D. Rodriguez who says, along with medical advances, it was Cameron's determination to survive that helped make the surgery a success.

"In the end, it's all about the patient. Cameron has put in the work and has made the necessary commitments," he says.

Cameron's transplant was the third carried out by Dr Rodriguez and he says the relatively short time in which Cameron had lived with his injuries was also a major factor in his recovery.

"Cameron has not lived with his injury for a decade or longer like most other face transplant recipients have," he says.

"As a result, he has not had to deal with many of the long-term psychosocial issues which often lead to issues like severe depression, substance abuse, and other potentially harmful behaviours."

During the surgery, the doctor transplanted and reconstructed Cameron's upper and lower jaw, including all 32 teeth and gums.

The roof and floor of his mouth, lower eyelids and nose were replaced and his tongue needed reconstruction.

The centre says the operation was the most technologically advanced face transplant and was the first use of a 3D-printed donor facial mask in the US.

'My son is helping Cameron live a better life'

The donor was 23-year-old Will Fisher, a chess champion, aspiring writer and filmmaker.

"My son's death was a tragedy," says Will's mum Sally.

"I am thankful that, in honouring his decision, we were able to give life to others, and especially that Will and Dr Rodriguez have given Cameron and his family a chance to recapture their dreams.

"Being a part of this experience has been a source of strength for me during a very difficult time.

"I don't think I would have survived Will's death if not for Cameron. Cameron has his whole life ahead of him - and I love the idea that Willie is helping him have a better life."

Cameron paid tribute to Will and the support of the Fisher family during his speech at the hospital's press conference.

"I want Sally and her family to know how much my family and I appreciate their gift and I'll always honour Will's legacy," he says.

"There have been so many amazing advances in surgery. I'm living proof of that. But it only happens because of special people like Will and his family."

articles.title: 15-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Telangana's Siddipet; 7 arrested, including 3 minors, in POCSO case
articles.summary: Seven, including three minors, arrested in Siddipet POCSO case over alleged sexual assault of a 15-year-old on Dasara; remanded to custody.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Seven persons, including three minors, were arrested and remanded to judicial custody in a Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) case involving the alleged sexual assault of a 15-year-old girl in Siddipet district. The incident took place on Dasara when the girl’s parents had gone out for agricultural work, police said.According to Maddur sub-inspector MD Asif, the seven accused allegedly took her to a neighbouring village on Dasara and left her back in her village the following morning.When the girl did not return home through the night, her parents began enquiring about her whereabouts. They later learnt that she had allegedly been taken away and sexually assaulted. The girl reportedly identified the accused, following which her father lodged a complaint with the police.Police registered a case under the Pocso Act, arrested all seven accused and produced them before a court, which remanded them to judicial custody.Asif said the identities of the accused were being withheld because the victim was a minor and three of the accused were also minors. He added that drug tests were conducted on all seven accused using rapid test kits under the supervision of the Husnabad ACP. articles.title: Ruins of city hall a symbol of France divided by protests
articles.summary: Younger Limoges residents see the destruction of their town hall as unfortunate collateral damage in a wider movement. For others, the fire was an unacceptable tragedy.
articles.body:
"It is a historical tragedy for France, not just Limoges".

Just six months into his mayoral term, it is hard to imagine Guillaume Guérin having a more momentous week.

We talk next to what became the defining image of last week's nationwide protests: the still impressive, yet fragile exterior of his town's 19th-Century town hall, charred from a fire.

The sight of its wooden clock tower collapsing into the flames drew widespread shock and anger, and Guérin, who was in tears when he first saw the scale of the damage this week, believes the reaction is "legitimate and completely understandable".

What is apparent from the array of flowers and sombre onlookers gathered at the hall's entrance, is that this is a town mourning the loss, or at the least the harm inflicted on its most iconic and, frankly, most beautiful building.

Guérin blames the damage on the French hard left, "supported by rioters". Two men have been arrested, a 66-year-old, as well as another suspect who is 34. Prosecutors say they have links to "radical-left networks".

Limoges' conservative mayor claims he has received a message of support from US Vice President JD Vance, but not Emmanual Macron, his own, outgoing president.

"What happened here will have an influence on the upcoming presidential election. This country is not doing well at all," he says.

For weeks, hundreds of thousands of people, mostly young, have engaged in protests that have only increased in size and scope. What started off as a demonstration over the poor state of high schools has expanded to a general frustration, even anger, over how challenging and expensive life has become.

In the backdrop is a daunting fiscal deficit, one of the biggest in Europe, and political candidates from across the spectrum claiming to have the answers ahead of presidential elections in six months' time.

In the middle is a centrist government, which is short on solutions, a majority in the National Assembly and time. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu visited Limoges on Friday evening.

Officials have banned demonstrations in various cities and promised to boost police numbers over the weekend to avoid a repeat of the rioting. That includes in Limoges, where overnight curfews have been announced, along with a limit on gatherings to 10 people in the centre.

Proud as the French are of their politics being rooted in street demonstrations, many in Limoges felt the town hall's destruction went far beyond the parameters of reasonable protest. But not everyone.

Whether the destruction of Limoges town hall changes the course and tone of an increasingly polarised political debate depends on who you ask.

"Of course it was really sad, it's a symbol of the republic, but what is more important: a town hall or people living in poverty?" asks Alexander, 24.

It is student night at the Lord John pub, and Alexander is one of several wearing a faluche, a colourful, traditional French student beret. Many chatting under the mist from their vapes took part in the demonstrations last weekend.

I ask Alexander whether the widespread looting and fires seen last weekend, with €500,000 (£420,000) of reported damage in Limoges, helped his argument?

"For some people it's a catastrophe and some things are not acceptable," he admits.

Jade, a 19-year-old, medical student, has a similar opinion: "I think burning the town hall is sad, but it's not the saddest part of the protests."

She complains of having to live on €300 per month.

"I feel we are not respected as young adults."

Their views on the town hall's fate are not replicated in Limoges' imposing market halls, where neat, narrow timbers sitting upon studded steel girders have been painted a duck-egg blue, using the same engineering approach as the Eiffel Tower.

This has been a "week of chaos" that 63-year-old Jean Roger Faucher would like to forget.

In a region renowned for producing beef, his family has run his fishmonger stool here for more than a century.

"It left us stunned," he says. "I got married in the town hall, so it had an unimaginable effect on us."

Asked whether he had sympathy for the protesters, Faucher said it was more complicated than that.

"On one side you have people with grievances you can understand, but from the moment there is vandalism and the lives of local residents are put at risk, then we can't accept it," he adds.

Among those tending to their iced displays of fresh produce or quietly sipping a steaming coffee, there is a desire for the temperature of the demonstrations to decrease.

"Of course, life is expensive!' says Pascale Vuylsteke, 59. "Life isn't all a calm river, it's complicated, but we grit our teeth and we work," she tells me leaning over shelves of butchered pork.

Pascale says she works 100 hours a week and struggles to understand why so many others have taken to the streets so easily.

Limoges has found itself at the heart of social action before. In the 19th Century, around the time the town hall was built, the development of its industries, notably in porcelain, led to it becoming a major centre for the French labour movement.

In 2026, the town sits centre-stage once more in a political rupture, although there is a broad hope that the loss of a prominent piece of its history will steer the demonstrations away from destruction and back to debate.

With France's political polarisation set to continue and further protests planned, it is a scenario far from assured.

articles.title: Video: Gunmen storm Jordan church during funeral, killing 7 and wounding 40 mourners
articles.summary: At least seven people were killed and 40 others injured after gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, authorities said.
articles.body: At least seven people were killed and 40 others injured after gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, authorities said. The attack took place in the southern city of Karak, around 180 kilometres south of the capital, Amman.Jordan's government described the attackers as unknown assailants and said investigations were moving ahead at full speed. It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed.Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.Videos recorded by witnesses showed shattered glass and pools of blood on the church floor.Dorgham Halasa, who was attending the funeral, said the shooting began around 15 minutes after the service started, triggering panic among mourners.“It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire,” Halasa told news agency AP.He did not see the attackers himself, but said other people had reported seeing four gunmen. The Associated Press could not independently verify how many people were involved, and Jordan's security services did not immediately provide further details.Jordan declares three days of mourningJordan announced three days of national mourning following the killings, the kingdom's Petra News Agency reported.Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of the injured were in critical condition.King Abdullah II condemned the attack in a post on X, pledging a strong response and offering condolences to the victims' families.Jordan “will confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties,” the king said, while extending his “deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded.”Prime Minister Jafar Hassan also addressed the incident during a security meeting in Karak on Friday evening. He blamed the attack on terrorist ideology and blind extremism, adding that those responsible would be punished and legal action would be taken against people seeking to spread extremism.The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, a city with a minority Christian population.Regional leaders condemn attackThe killings drew condemnation from across the region, including Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and Oman.Ahmed al-Tayeb, the grand imam of Al-Azhar in Cairo, offered condolences to the victims' families and described the shooting as a “heinous terrorist attack”. Al-Azhar is one of the most influential institutions in Sunni Islam.Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein also spoke to his Jordanian counterpart and expressed Baghdad's support for Amman.Hussein's office said he “affirmed Iraq’s solidarity with Jordan in the face of terrorism”.United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the attack, describing violence during a funeral as “especially heinous”, his spokesman Stephane Dujarric said.“The secretary-general also calls for all those responsible to be found and to be held to account,” Dujarric added.Karak has witnessed deadly attacks in the past. In 2016, gunmen ambushed police at several locations in the city, including a Crusader castle popular with tourists. The attacks killed 10 people, including seven police officers, and wounded dozens.Jordanian security forces eventually killed the attackers after a prolonged standoff.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Bibi Perigosa’ é suspeita de ordenar ataque e ameaças a mãe e filha | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigada foi presa em flagrante no bairro Messejana, em Fortaleza. Segundo a Polícia Civil, ela teria determinado a saída forçada de moradores do bairro Cajazeiras.
articles.summary: Investigada foi presa em flagrante no bairro Messejana, em Fortaleza. Segundo a Polícia Civil, ela teria determinado a saída forçada de moradores do bairro Cajazeiras.
articles.body:
Carla Germana Sales, conhecida como "Bibi Perigosa", é apontada pela polícia como a responsável por ordenar a expulsão de mãe e filha de duas casas na comunidade Barreirão, no bairro Cajazeiras, em Fortaleza . A suspeita, que tem 35 anos, foi presa nesta quinta-feira (22) no bairro Messejana.

A casa de uma das vítimas foi alvo de disparos de arma de fogo e de ameaças deixadas por pichações nas paredes, que diziam que elas tinham 24 horas para abandonar os imóveis. A expulsão das moradoras ocorreu na terça-feira (20).

Bibi é suspeita de chefiar a Massa, um grupo criminoso de origem cearense, e ordenar a expulsão de moradores de suas casas. Ela foi presa pelo crime de domínio social estruturado.

O g1 não localizou a defesa de Carla Germana Sales. Ao ser interrogada pela polícia, ela reconheceu que conhece as vítimas, mas negou ter cometido os crimes e ter o apelido de 'Bibi Perigosa' - apesar de ela ter uma tatuagem com o nome 'Bibi' em um braço.

A mulher presa pela Polícia Civil do Ceará possui antecedentes criminais por roubo a pessoa, adulteração de sinal identificador de veículo, homicídio, corrupção de menores e participação em organização criminosa.

‘Bibi Perigosa’ é suspeita de ordenar ataque a tiros a casa, pichação com ameaça e expulsão de mãe e filha em Fortaleza. — Foto: Reprodução

Conforme documentos obtidos pelo g1, uma das vítimas disse à polícia que morava em uma casa na comunidade do Barreirão, localizada no bairro Cajazeiras; e sua mãe morava em outra, ao lado. Na parte de cima dos imóveis, há outras residências que são alugadas.

Bibi teria pedido que mãe e filha alugassem os imóveis disponíveis para pessoas indicadas por elas . As vítimas se recusaram, pois, anteriormente, já haviam alugado os imóveis para pessoas ligadas à Bibi, e confrontos entre facções criminosas haviam ocorrido próximo às casas, até com disparos atingindo as paredes das residências.

Em um dos casos, os moradores das casas teriam até reagido aos disparos, iniciando troca de tiros e aumentando o medo das vítimas pela própria segurança e integridade física.

Após a recusa, a mulher teria começado a ser ameaçada por Bibi, que alegou que a vítima "não estava colaborando com a facção criminosa atuante na região". O grupo criminoso atuante na região é a Massa.

No dia 20 de outubro, a casa da mulher foi alvo de disparos de arma de fogo e uma ameaça foi pichada no imóvel: "TEM 24H PRA SAIR".

Apontada como chefe de facção, 'Bibi Perigosa' é presa no Ceará suspeita de ordenar expulsões de moradores no bairro Cajazeiras. — Foto: Divulgação/SSPDS

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSPDS) confirmou que houve pessoas deslocadas na região, mas não informou a quantidade nem a motivação. O caso é investigado pela Delegacia de Repressão às Ações Criminosas Organizadas (Draco).

Esta é pelo menos a segunda ocorrência de expulsão de moradores na comunidade do Barreirão em 2026. Em julho deste ano, vários moradores deixaram suas casas após ameaças realizadas por integrantes de uma facção criminosa que tenta dominar a região. A área vive uma situação de conflito entre facção cearense Massa e a facção carioca Comando Vermelho.

A comunidade do Barreirão também é a mesma onde ocorreu, em 2018, a Chacina das Cajazeiras, considerada a maior da história do Ceará, na qual foram mortas 14 pessoas devido à disputa entre grupos criminosos.

Por meio de nota, a secretaria disse que ações de policiamento na região foram realizadas por equipes da Polícia Militar e que as denúncias de deslocamento forçado "que chegam ao seu conhecimento são devidamente apuradas e acompanhadas".

"No Ceará, foi iniciado, em julho de 2025, um protocolo integrado entre as Forças de Segurança do Estado para combater a prática, registrada em vários estados do país, e que é parte da forma de atuação de grupos criminosos. Os crimes vêm sendo combatidos a partir do mapeamento, monitoramento e prisão desses suspeitos. Como resultado desse trabalho, de julho de 2025 até agora, 151 capturas por deslocamento foram registradas no estado", destacou a secretaria.

O concurso 3.074 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 230 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre excepcionalmente às 21h deste sábado (24) devido ao segundo turno das eleições de 2026.

No concurso do última quinta-feira (22), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

Para alé da Mega, outras seis loterias também foram adiantadas para hoje. São elas:

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Da textura ao acabamento, pedras ganham novas leituras na arquitetura  | G1
articles.standfirst: Quartzitos, travertinos e outras referências naturais inspiram superfícies para diferentes ambientes e aplicações.
articles.summary: Quartzitos, travertinos e outras referências naturais inspiram superfícies para diferentes ambientes e aplicações.
articles.body:
A busca por ambientes com mais conexão com elementos naturais têm influenciado desde a escolha das cores até as superfícies que revestem a casa. Nesse cenário, as pedras aparecem com novas interpretações e ocupam diferentes espaços da arquitetura, deixando de estar associadas apenas a pisos e bancadas para avançar sobre paredes, painéis, fachadas e áreas externas.

Essa expansão trouxe também um repertório maior de desenhos e acabamentos. Quartzitos, travertinos, limestones e rochas de aparência mais bruta servem de referência para revestimentos com características bastante distintas. Alguns são marcados por veios intensos e contrastes de cor; outros apresentam desenhos lineares, tonalidades suaves ou texturas mais evidentes. Entender essas diferenças ajuda a determinar o papel que a superfície terá no projeto, seja como ponto de destaque ou como base para os demais elementos do ambiente.

Marcas, variações e desenhos inspirados nas rochas dão ao Neolithic uma aparência natural que se destaca em grandes superfícies — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

O Neolithic Natural 120x120, da Roca Cerámica, representa uma interpretação mais expressiva desse universo. A coleção busca inspiração nas transformações provocadas pela passagem do tempo sobre as rochas, trazendo marcas e veios que dão movimento à superfície. No grande formato, o desenho ganha espaço para aparecer com menos interferência das juntas e pode ser explorado em pisos, paredes, painéis e outras superfícies internas.

Já o travertino segue por outro caminho visual. Seus desenhos característicos, geralmente mais lineares, e as nuances de tonalidade criam uma superfície de leitura mais suave. Essa diferença permite utilizar referências de pedra em ambientes próximos sem necessariamente produzir o mesmo efeito, escolhendo uma linguagem mais marcante ou mais discreta de acordo com a proposta.

Inspirado no travertino italiano, o Navona Natural ABS leva a aparência da pedra para espaços externos com acabamento adequado a esse tipo de aplicação — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Inspirado no mármore travertino italiano, o Navona Natural ABS 120x120, da Roca Cerámica, mostra como essa referência pode avançar para áreas externas. A versão ABS possui acabamento desenvolvido para esses espaços e baixa absorção de água, permitindo aplicações em varandas e outros ambientes sujeitos às condições externas. A tonalidade e o desenho da superfície também favorecem a combinação com madeira, vegetação e elementos presentes no paisagismo.

Nas lojas Vilarejo, a comparação das peças em diferentes dimensões ajuda a perceber características que nem sempre aparecem em imagens ou pequenas amostras. Aproximar superfícies, observar desenhos e avaliar acabamentos permite entender melhor como cada referência poderá participar da composição antes da definição do material.

Quartzito, travertino, limestone ou uma pedra de aspecto mais bruto podem partir da mesma inspiração natural, mas não contam a mesma história dentro de um ambiente. É justamente essa diversidade que ampliou o espaço das pedras na arquitetura e abriu novas possibilidades para levá-las do piso às paredes e das áreas internas ao exterior da casa.

articles.title: Saiba como foi retirada de carro sem freio de prédio em caracol no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo estava sem funcionar e precisou percorrer rampa em espiral para deixar prédio em Novo Hamburgo. Dono sonhava com o veículo desde a infância e mobilizou amigos para o resgate.
articles.summary: Veículo estava sem funcionar e precisou percorrer rampa em espiral para deixar prédio em Novo Hamburgo. Dono sonhava com o veículo desde a infância.
articles.body:
Retirar um carro antigo de um estacionamento já pode ser um desafio. Quando o veículo está sem freios, com o motor parado e estacionado no nono andar de um prédio com acesso em caracol , a tarefa exige ainda mais cuidado.

Foi essa a situação enfrentada por Tiago Fabiano Corrêa Pacheco, de 46 anos, proprietário de um Ford Galaxie 500 fabricado em 1971 que permaneceu durante 17 anos guardado em um edifício de Novo Hamburgo , na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre .

O veículo foi comprado em 2021 por Tiago, que conhecia o automóvel desde a infância. Conheça história abaixo.

Para conseguir trazer o automóvel ao térreo, foi necessário montar uma operação especial . Como o carro não tinha condições de se movimentar por conta própria, Tiago reuniu amigos para auxiliar na descida pela estrutura em espiral do prédio .

O principal apoio veio de um jipe com tração 4x4, utilizado como medida de segurança durante todo o percurso. O veículo servia para conter o Galaxie e possibilitar uma reação imediata caso fosse necessário interromper a descida.

Apesar da complexidade da manobra, tudo ocorreu conforme o planejado.

"Deu tudo certo, descemos de primeira, mas foi uma grande festa a retirada do carro", relembra o proprietário.

Depois de finalmente deixar o prédio, o Galaxie passou pelos primeiros cuidados antes da restauração. O carro foi encaminhado para uma garagem, onde recebeu limpeza e preparação para a avaliação mecânica .

Na sequência, diversos componentes passaram por revisão, entre eles os freios, os rolamentos, a bomba-d'água, o radiador, a carburação e o alternador .

"O motor não precisa fazer nada. O carro é mais do que eu esperava", afirma Tiago.

Carro que ficou 17 anos estacionado estava no 9º andar de prédio, sem freios e motor não funcionava: 'Foi uma grande festa a retirada' — Foto: Tiago Pacheco/Arquivo pessoal

A relação do dono com o automóvel é antiga. De acordo com Tiago, o Galaxie estava em um estacionamento pelo qual passava no caminho entre sua casa e a escola . Na década de 1990, entre os 11 e 12 anos, ele observava o carro durante o trajeto. Porém, depois o automóvel foi retirado do local e ele ficou 30 anos sem vê-lo.

Décadas depois, durante uma visita a outro estacionamento com o sogro, Tiago reconheceu o veículo. O Galaxie estava um andar acima do local onde os dois verificavam outro automóvel.

"Eu digo: 'Esse carro é o carro que eu via no colégio'. Vamos tentar comprar", lembra.

Tiago conseguiu o contato da família proprietária, mas inicialmente não houve acordo. A viúva do dono demonstrou interesse na negociação, porém o filho queria ficar com o veículo. A venda ocorreu apenas quando o herdeiro procurou o sogro de Tiago para oferecer o automóvel.

"Aí comprei ele em 2021. Depois de 30 anos, fui comprar o carro", relata.

Jornal de 1988 foi achado dentro do veículo

Ao receber a chave, Tiago procurou objetos que ajudassem a identificar por quanto tempo o veículo havia permanecido parado . Entre os itens encontrados estava um jornal de 10 de outubro de 1988 .

"Na época se lavava o carro e colocava o jornal embaixo do tapete para tirar a umidade. Então, muitos usavam isso. Então, acredito que em 1988 foi lavado e foi posto ali", relata.

Outro papel, datado de 2004, também foi encontrado no interior do veículo. De acordo com Tiago, o Galaxie deixou o primeiro estacionamento naquele ano e foi transferido para o prédio onde permaneceu até 2021 .

Atualmente, 5 anos após a compra, o carro aguarda a etapa de pintura. O proprietário pretende continuar com o veículo e levá-lo a eventos de colecionadores.

"Agora, eu quero terminar ele e depois vou seguir usando, quero fazer mais história com ele, quero levar em eventos, expor o carro, mas pretendo ficar com ele", conclui.

articles.title: Jornalistas agredidos em Belém: equipe apurava denúncia em porto | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o sindicato da categoria, equipe do Portal Cidade091 foi agredida fisicamente no Porto Bom Jesus. Profissionais apuravam denúncias de recusa de passagens gratuitas para eleitores no segundo turno.
articles.summary: Jornalistas agredidos em Belém foram atacados no Porto Bom Jesus enquanto apuravam denúncias sobre a recusa de passagens gratuitas para eleitores no segundo turno.
articles.body:
Jornalistas são agredidos ao apurar denúncia de recusa de passagens gratuitas para eleitores em Belém. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Os jornalistas Lucas Contente e Gustavo Baima, do Portal Cidade091 , foram agredidos fisicamente e tiveram equipamento de trabalho retirado à força nesta sexta-feira (23), no Porto Bom Jesus, em Belém , segundo o Sindicato dos Jornalistas do Pará (Sinjor-PA).

A equipe apurava denúncias de que a Navegação Bom Jesus estaria se recusando a conceder passagens gratuitas a eleitores no segundo turno das eleições. O g1 tenta contato com a empresa.

A reportagem tratava de denúncias de descumprimento do Decreto Estadual nº 5.715/2026, que garante gratuidade no transporte intermunicipal para eleitores no segundo turno.

De acordo com o Sinjor-PA, a ação foi comandada por Raimundo Rebelo, identificado pela entidade como diretor de operações da Navegação Bom Jesus. O Portal Cidade091 afirmou que integrantes da segurança privada também participaram das agressões.

Segundo o sindicato, os jornalistas foram expulsos do porto enquanto tentavam obter a versão da empresa sobre as denúncias.

“Durante a tentativa de obter a versão da empresa, os jornalistas foram expulsos do local. As imagens mostram a equipe sendo hostilizada, o equipamento de trabalho sendo retirado à força e as agressões físicas. Lucas Contente chega a ser derrubado no chão”, afirmou o Sinjor-PA.

O Sinjor-PA informou que acompanha o caso e colocou a assessoria jurídica à disposição dos profissionais para a adoção das medidas cabíveis e a responsabilização dos envolvidos.

A entidade repudiou as agressões e destacou a liberdade de imprensa como uma das bases da democracia e um direito constitucional

Em manifestação, o Portal Cidade091 também condenou a violência contra os profissionais .

“É inaceitável que profissionais de imprensa sejam submetidos à violência e à intimidação por buscar esclarecimentos de interesse público. O exercício do jornalismo é um direito fundamental, essencial à democracia, e nenhuma tentativa de silenciamento pode ser tolerada. E não vai!”, afirmou o portal.

articles.title: MrBeast invests $250,000 for 55% stake in AI-powered Ball 2 on Shark Tank
articles.summary: MrBeast has built a career on turning unusual ideas into viral sensations.
articles.body: MrBeast has built a career on turning unusual ideas into viral sensations. Now, the YouTube star is betting that the same formula can sell an everyday object with an unexpected twist. During his debut on Shark Tank, Jimmy Donaldson backed Ball 2, an AI-powered toy that promises to make ordinary play more interactive. The $250,000 investment came despite doubts from other investors, who questioned whether technology alone could convince customers to choose this ball over countless cheaper alternatives. The deal puts MrBeast's marketing instincts to the test, with the product's future depending on whether its novelty can attract lasting demand.MrBeast backs AI-powered Ball 2 with a $250,000 Shark Tank dealEntrepreneurs Andrew Brown and Kevin Langdon pitched Ball 2 as a new take on a familiar toy. Unlike a standard foam ball, their product contains sensors that track its movement when users roll, throw or bounce it. The data connects to a companion app, where artificial intelligence can help create games based on how people use the ball.The idea aims to turn simple physical activity into an interactive experience. Instead of relying on a fixed set of rules, players can use the app to introduce new challenges and change how they play.During a demonstration, MrBeast and fellow investor Lori Greiner competed to see who could shake the ball more. Donaldson won and appeared pleasantly surprised by the result.“It worked way better than I was expecting it to work,” said Donaldson after getting his shake on, “that was cool.”His enthusiasm stood out as several investors questioned the product's appeal. Kevin Langdon even acknowledged the challenge of selling something that looks like an ordinary ball on a shop shelf.“If you put this next to another ball on a shelf it’s a tough sell,” admits Langdon.MrBeast ultimately offered $250,000 for a 55% stake in the company. The cousins accepted, celebrating the deal with a shout of “beast ball!”Why MrBeast's Ball 2 investment faces questions over consumer demandThe biggest challenge for Ball 2 may not be its technology. It is convincing families that they need it.Balls are familiar, affordable and easy to use. Adding sensors and AI may attract curious buyers, but parents will still want to know whether the extra features justify the price. The product must also offer enough variety to keep children interested after the initial excitement fades.Kevin O'Leary, known as Mr. Wonderful, remained unconvinced by the pitch. His huge online audience and experience creating attention-grabbing videos could give Ball 2 the exposure it needs. A viral campaign could turn an unfamiliar toy into a popular gift, particularly among younger fans.However, attention does not always translate into repeat sales. articles.title: UK state pension: How does it compare with other countries?
articles.summary: Do British pensioners have it better or worse than those in other countries?
articles.body:
Getting older is something few of us want to think about. Yet how we fund our later years, and how much we'll get, has been a hot topic.

The triple lock formula - state pensions increasing by the greatest of 2.5%, earnings growth, or inflation - means those benefits have risen far faster than the earnings of workers since its introduction in 2011.

But as housing costs have also been rising fast, pensioner poverty has actually increased slightly in the last decade.

Nevertheless, even if you take those costs into consideration, pensioners are less likely to be in relative poverty - that is, having to get by on less than 60% of the income of the typical household - than families with children or working-age people.

And funding the triple lock has already cost the state billions more than initially envisaged. With that cost set to balloon further, the debate over whether that is sustainable, or fair, has raged for a while.

Andy Burnham intends to start a new system in a few years, which would see the state pension increase by at least inflation or 2.5%, and remove the automatic annual link with average earnings. It will likely mean less generous increases, although it will keep track with earnings growth over the longer term.

But are pensioners being short-changed in other ways? How do we compare with other countries?

One way of measuring that is to look at how generous the typical pension is relative to workers' average earnings - the replacement rate.

The OECD considers the outlook for those born at the start of the millennium in different countries on average wages, and assumes the pension system as it existed in 2022 is in place.

On that basis, looking at the basic state pension, retirement benefits in the UK look low compared with other wealthy countries.

And that is even when you consider that our system compels workers to be automatically enrolled in occupational schemes.

If you consider both of those, then after tax, UK retirement benefits would be 54.2% of average UK earnings, compared with an average of 63.2% across wealthy countries.

Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

State pension likely to top £13,000 a year

What is the triple lock and why are people talking about it?

But then there is income from other occupational and personal pensions, which are more prevalent in the UK. Include those and the gap narrows.

However, that does also mean that those relying on just the state pension for their incomes are a fair bit worse off than many retired people elsewhere.

So does that make the case for boosting spending on public pensions in the UK?

Well, the amount spent on the state pension is set to top £150bn a year, the single most expensive benefit to fund.

But other figures from the OECD show that the UK state spends a lower amount on total retirement benefits, relative to the size of its economy, than the average wealthy country.

Firstly, this is about political choices, and the UK chooses to dedicate larger amounts to items such as universal healthcare.

And secondly, with ageing populations, the OECD reckons the amount needed for pensions may be set to soar in many nations by 2060 (the exceptions largely being those that are deploying changes).

Its predictions for the UK are likely to rise by less under the revised triple lock system being put in place by Andy Burnham but it may still mean more borrowing.

As it is, £1 in every £13 the UK government spends is to pay the interest on existing debt. And countries with more generous pensions, such as Italy, have faced pressure to reform.

So in many ways, with auto-enrolment into workplace pensions, the UK appears to be ahead of the game in insisting on universal privately funded pensions for workers. But that system raises another issue: the gender pension gap.

The gender pension gap is the difference between the average pension income of men and women aged 65 and over, as a percentage of men's average pension income.

It found that the typical gap in most wealthy countries is around 22.8% in favour of men.

But in the UK women typically get a pension that is a third less than what a man gets - in the main, due to the reliance on private pensions - although it should be noted that the most recent data the OECD has for the UK is for 2021.

Women are more likely to have received lower pay over the course of their working lives, taken career breaks or worked part time. And the hit to pension pots can be stark.

So step back and look at the big picture and British pensioners - and those who have yet to retire - may feel others have it better elsewhere.

But the message from all of this isn't to dwell on outrage but to take action.

The state pension has become more generous over the years, but if you want to enjoy the same kind of retirement as those elsewhere, get saving.

That is - if you can, and if you haven't left it too late.

articles.title: FBI detains gangster Himanshu Bhau, India may get custody soon
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US, after a four-year-long manhunt.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Himanshu Bhau, one of north India's most wanted gangsters, is learnt to have been detained in the US, after a four-year-long manhunt. Subject of a red notice from the Interpol, Bhau, a rival of Lawrence Bishnoi group, is wanted for multiple cases off shootings, killings and multi-crore extortions in Delhi and Haryana.Bhau, sources said, was apprehended by FBI in Las Vegas/Nevada region following inputs from Indian agencies. He is likely to be handed over to Indian law enforcement agencies, who have been chasing him since 2022, in the coming days, sources said.In his early twenties, Bhau is one of north India's most notorious young fugitives, heading an organised crime syndicate. He has been a headache for cops in Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan with back-to-back killings, including three sensational murders in Delhi, this year."He belongs to Ritoli in the Rohtak district of Haryana and had got involved in crimes while still in school. He first entered police records in 2020 following a botched killing attempt involving a localized dispute in his native village," an investigator recalled.Since he was a minor at the time of apprehension, cops detained him and sent him to a juvenile observation home in Hisar. However, his stay there was brief; he engineered an audacious escape from the facility, casting aside any prospect of rehabilitation and plunging headfirst into a career of violent crime that soon expanded far beyond rural Haryana.Operating in close coordination with seasoned syndicates, including the Neeraj Bawana and Naveen Bali gangs, Bhau rapidly built a formidable network spanning Rohtak, Jhunjhunu, Sonipat, and the National Capital Region of Delhi.As law enforcement agencies closed in on his local footprints, including a series of high-profile murders in his home district in March 2022, he managed to orchestrate an escape from the country."In 2022, he executed three killings in a span of 24 days in March. The same year, using a passport obtained through fraudulent documents, Bhau slipped across international borders, initially fleeing to Dubai before moving on to European safe havens like Portugal, from where he continued to remotely direct his syndicate," said an investigator.Despite being a fugitive with Red Corner Notices and heavy cash rewards issued by multiple police jurisdictions and the National Investigation Agency, he leveraged encrypted messaging applications to command local shooters.He is suspected to have reached US through the "Dunkey Route" in late 2024-early 2025.His syndicate has claimed responsibility for a string of high-profile shootings, extortions, and contract killings that terrorised businessmen and shook law enforcement.Among his syndicate's most brazen operations was the daring killing of a rival at a prominent fast-food chain outlet in West Delhi's Rajouri Garden.His network has also targeted commercial establishments, unleashing dozens of rounds of gunfire at car showrooms in Naraina and Tilak Nagar alongside multi-million rupee extortion demands directed at builders, real estate developers, and local traders across Delhi-NCR.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads; factories stay shut for days, owners count their losses
articles.summary: GURGAON: The power strike that crippled the city and other parts of Haryana for two days was called off late on Friday evening after chief minister Nayab
articles.body: GURGAON: The power strike that crippled the city and other parts of Haryana for two days was called off late on Friday evening after chief minister Nayab Singh Saini assured electricity department employees that no private parallel power distribution licences would be allowed anywhere in the state.The shutdown had left many homes facing long outages and disrupted water supply, while bringing industrial production to a halt for more than 24 hours. Govt invoked Section 108(1) of Electricity Act, 2003 - which empowers it to issue policy directions to the state electricity regulator on matters of public interest - and asked it not to create or operationalise such licences.The order came four days after Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) granted Eleven Power Pvt Ltd a 25-year licence to distribute electricity alongside Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) in Gurgaon and Nuh.Representatives of Haryana Joint Action Committee said Saini and energy minister Anil Vij heard them out and apprised them of the steps being taken by govt to oppose the granting of parallel licences.The state said it was not questioning the correctness of HERC's findings in its order, but raised concerns over the private company's financial capacity, technical preparedness and ability to supply all consumers in its licensed area.It also flagged the risk of a private distributor choosing high-revenue consumers, potentially weakening cross-subsidy arrangements and leaving the state utility with existing power purchase commitments, stranded costs and duplicated infrastructure. These could increase the financial burden on DHBVN and consumers. The govt asked the HERC secretary to place the directive before the commission.Chief minister Saini also ordered officials to restore electricity immediately in all affected districts. Following his directions, Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd (HVPNL) managing director Aditya Dahiya and DHBVN and Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (UHBVN) managing director Vikram Singh met superintending and executive engineers and directed them to ensure uninterrupted supply.The strike had caused widespread disruption before the settlement. Outages stretched beyond 40 hours in some neighbourhoods, residents blocked Gurgaon-Pataudi Road, Railway Road and Basai Road, bringing traffic to a standstill until cops intervened. Water shortages, exhausted inverters and disrupted work routines added to the distress.Old Gurgaon bore much of the brunt, particularly colonies along Railway Road and Basai Road. In Ashok Vihar Phase 1, power went off on Thursday morning and remained unavailable in most homes until late Friday. Rajendra Park and Vishnu Garden reported outages from 10am on Thursday, while residents of Surat Nagar faced similar conditions. Hundreds of homes in sectors 4, 7 and 7 Extension, as well as New Palam Vihar, Sai Kunj and Chandan Vihar, reported prolonged cuts.The disruption also crippled water supply as electric pumps stopped working. In Hari Nagar on Khandsa Road, residents protested outside the Sector 34 power house on Thursday night after supply failed on Wednesday.DHBVN received around 9,500 complaints through its toll-free number over two days, including about 4,500 on Friday. By Friday evening, 32 feeders were still reported shut. Each feeder serves an average of 1,700 households, highlighting the scale of the problem.Several societies switched to generator power, which residents said cost around Rs 30 per unit. These included Hero Homes in Sector 104, Godrej Frontier in Sector 80, Chintels Paradiso in Sector 109 and Emerald Hills among others.Prolonged generator use also raised concerns about pollution.Affordable housing societies without generator backup suffered especially badly. Inverters ran out, water purifiers stopped working and families turned to bottled water. Santosh Singh of Pareena Laxmi Apartments in Sector 99A, home to around 650 families, said power had been unavailable since 6pm on Thursday.Factories stay shut for days, owners count their lossesThe industrial belt took a massive hit from three days of power cuts, with industry leaders estimating production losses of more than Rs 20,000 crore.Textile, auto components and food units, along with export houses, halted operations as outages disrupted manufacturing schedules, delayed customer orders and put delivery commitments at risk. Businesses also warned of damage to machinery and raw materials, while thousands of daily wagers lost earnings during the festive season.The strike was called off late on Friday evening after talks between employee representatives and energy minister Anil Vij. The disruption, however, had already hit production schedules, delayed customer orders and put delivery commitments at risk.Two industry bodies — Gurgaon Chamber of Commerce & Industry (GCCI) and Progressive Federation of Trade & Industry (PFTI) — wrote to chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, seeking urgent intervention to restore power and limit further losses.In its letter on Friday, GCCI said outages that began on the night of Oct 21 had severely affected industrial and commercial activity. Units were unable to maintain scheduled operations or meet customer deadlines, adding to the financial burden of lost production.The chamber also warned that interruptions could have consequences beyond the immediate loss of output. Sensitive machinery, production processes and raw materials could be damaged by power disruptions, while missed dispatch deadlines could affect contractual commitments.Some businesses tried using diesel generator (DG) sets, but GCCI said this was neither economical nor technically feasible over an extended period. Higher fuel bills added to operating costs, while generator capacity and technical limitations prevented many units from running their entire electrical load continuously.GCCI urged the state govt and power authorities to prioritise industrial feeders, manufacturing clusters and critical commercial areas. It also sought emergency contingency arrangements, better coordination among officials and reliable updates on restoration timelines so businesses could plan production and dispatches.PFTI, in a letter dated Oct 22, said the strike had left industrial operations stalled and workers idle in several areas. The timing had made matters worse. Businesses and workers usually depend on the festive season for higher production, earnings, incentives and bonuses.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Fire engulfs Hitler’s teahouse ‘Eagle’s Nest’ in Germany; man arrested on arson suspicion
articles.summary: A fire broke out at the historic Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle’s Nest, near Berchtesgaden in Germany’s Bavaria region on Friday evening, with
articles.body: A fire broke out at the historic Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle’s Nest, near Berchtesgaden in Germany’s Bavaria region on Friday evening, with police suspecting arson and arresting a man in connection with the incident.The alarm was raised shortly after 9pm local time, and emergency services rushed to the site on Kehlstein mountain. The building was already engulfed in flames when firefighters and police arrived, German newspaper BILD reported.A police spokesperson told BILD that arson was suspected. Officers heading to the site encountered a motorcyclist and alerted the fire brigade following behind them. The man was stopped and arrested, the spokesperson said.However, it remains unclear whether the arrested man was involved in starting the fire. The exact cause of the blaze is yet to be established.No injuries had been reported at the time of the report, and authorities believed that nobody was inside the building when the fire broke out.What is the Eagle’s Nest?Perched at an altitude of 1,834 metres above Berchtesgaden, the Kehlsteinhaus was built in 1937-38 as a prestigious teahouse for Nazi leader Adolf Hitler. It was also intended to serve as a venue for receiving foreign guests and diplomats during the Nazi era.Hitler rarely visited the site, which was designed as a place for political representation away from public view. The building survived World War II largely unscathed and has operated as a mountain inn since 1952.Owned by the Free State of Bavaria, the historic site is now a popular tourist destination, housing a restaurant and exhibitions documenting its links to Nazi Germany.You use AI every day. articles.title: Severe flooding soaks Four Corners region, prompts rooftop rescues and evacuations
articles.summary: Severe flooding in the Four Corners region Friday led to rescues — some from rooftops — and impassable roads, with some residents told to evacuate low-lying areas of Colorado and New Mexico and others urged to stay where they are until water levels drop.
articles.body: FORT COLLINS, Colo. — Severe flooding in the Four Corners region Friday led to rescues — some from rooftops — and impassable roads, with some residents told to evacuate low-lying areas of Colorado and New Mexico and others urged to stay where they are until water levels drop. The flooding followed two months of heavy rains that ended a summer drought in the region where the boundaries of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet. Since Wednesday, a total of 4 inches had fallen in the already saturated area, with even more rain forecast for the weekend. Hundreds of people along the San Juan River in the biggest city in the area, Farmington, New Mexico, were told to evacuate. Downstream, residents of the vast Navajo Nation braced for floodwaters not expected to peak until late Friday or early Saturday. “Do not wait to make your evacuations. Make your preparations for yourselves, your families, as well as your animals,” Navajo Nation Deputy Police Chief Donnie Kee urged during a news conference. The crisis capped a week of severe weather in which rain swamped dozens of homes in Utah and tornadoes blew off roofs, knocked trees onto houses and downed power lines in Arizona. In New Mexico, more flooding ahead Rescuers used New Mexico National Guard boats, helicopters and amphibious vehicles Thursday night and into Friday to try to reach stranded residents, San Juan County spokesperson Devin Neeley said. “We’re picking people off of roofs and pulling people out of houses that have 3 or 4 feet (1-1.5 meters) of water in them, and there’s more water coming,” Neeley said. Rains stopped — at least temporarily — but rivers were still rising. “This is serious. We’re still sending deputies as I speak to get people out of their homes right now. In fact, our sheriff is damn near going to lose his home today,” Neeley said. Some 600 Farmington households were told to evacuate, city spokesperson Gina Intoppa said. Still higher water was on the way via the Animas River, a San Juan tributary that also flows south from rain-soaked Colorado, Farmington Police Chief Steve Hebbe said in the news conference. “People are not believing that it’s going to be as bad as it is. But you can see the water flow coming, you can see the surge coming,” Hebbe said, calling it a “once in a generation” event. In Utah In the city of Hurricane in far southwestern Utah, a shipping container drifting down a street gave way Friday to a mess of mud and debris to be cleaned up as people who had evacuated earlier in the week returned home. The risk shifted to Utah's southeast, where streams ran fast and high. Flood watches were in effect into the weekend, said Alex DeSmet, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Salt Lake City. Still, the Four Corners region could get more heavy rain this weekend, with up to half an inch (1 centimeter) forecast to fall in northwestern New Mexico. While parts of the Southwest are rocky with little vegetation and are naturally prone to flash flooding, the recent rains had saturated the ground and made widespread flooding more likely. The moisture was from the remnants of Pacific tropical systems that had come ashore, forecasters said. _

articles.title: In 2019, two founders launched vodka made from carbon dioxide; their startup later secured a US defence contract worth up to $65 million to develop synthetic-fuel technology
articles.summary: Air Company, the New York startup founded by Gregory Constantine and Stafford Sheehan in 2017, set out to demonstrate how carbon dioxide could be
articles.body: Air Company, the New York startup founded by Gregory Constantine and Stafford Sheehan in 2017, set out to demonstrate how carbon dioxide could be converted into useful products. Its early focus included vodka made using alcohol produced from carbon dioxide and hydrogen. The company later expanded its work towards industrial applications, including synthetic aviation fuel. In February 2023, the US Department of Defense’s Defense Innovation Unit announced a contract with a ceiling of $65 million to develop synthetic-fuel production technology for use in contested environments. AIRCO, as the company is now known, cited a $67 million contract for the same project in a March 2026 announcement. The public announcements do not explain the difference between the two figures, and neither should be mistaken for confirmation that the full amount has been paid.Gregory Constantine and Stafford Sheehan founded Air Company to turn carbon dioxide into useful productsAir Company was founded in 2017 by Constantine, a business and marketing executive, and Sheehan, a chemist with a doctorate from Yale University. Their expertise addressed different parts of the challenge: Constantine focused on building a business around the technology, while Sheehan developed the chemical process for converting carbon dioxide into useful products. The company’s approach was to use carbon dioxide as a feedstock rather than treating it solely as a waste product. Its technology combines carbon dioxide and hydrogen to produce alcohols and other chemicals. Those products can then be used in consumer goods or as building blocks for synthetic fuels.The founders initially introduced a consumer product to demonstrate the technology. In November 2019, Air Company launched Air Vodka, made using ethanol produced from carbon dioxide and hydrogen. The company presented it as a premium spirit and a demonstration of its conversion process. The vodka helped make an unfamiliar technology tangible to consumers. Instead of asking people to understand an industrial fuel-production process, the company could show them a product made using its underlying chemistry. However, the vodka was a demonstration of the technology, not evidence that the company had already solved the cost and production challenges involved in manufacturing aviation fuel at scale.Air Vodka, perfume and hand sanitiser helped demonstrate the technologyAir Company expanded beyond vodka into fragrance products and hand sanitiser. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the company shifted part of its production towards hand sanitiser, using its alcohol-production capabilities to meet demand for the product. The consumer business also gave the company a way to demonstrate that its technology could produce commercially usable materials. Producing a premium spirit, fragrance or sanitiser involves different requirements from producing aviation fuel, but the products drew on the company’s broader expertise in converting carbon dioxide into chemicals.The company subsequently focused more heavily on industrial applications, including synthetic fuels. This shift required moving beyond relatively small consumer-product batches towards systems capable of producing fuel in larger quantities. The distinction matters because making a product from captured carbon dioxide does not automatically make it carbon-negative. The overall environmental impact depends on factors including the source of the carbon dioxide, the hydrogen-production method, the energy used and the full lifecycle of the resulting fuel.The $65 million defence contract is intended to support synthetic fuel production in the fieldOn February 28, 2023, the Defense Innovation Unit announced that it had awarded Air Company a contract with a ceiling of $65 million under Project SynCE, short for Synthetic Fuels for the Contested Environment. The project involved the US Air Force, the Operational Energy Capability Improvement Fund, the Department of Energy and the US Army’s Office of the Chief of Engineers. According to the Defense Innovation Unit’s announcement, the project aims to develop technology that can produce synthetic fuels close to where they are needed. Military operations often depend on long supply chains involving ships, tanker aircraft and ground convoys. Those routes can become vulnerable during conflict, making fuel availability a logistical and operational concern.The proposed system is intended to produce drop-in synthetic fuels that can be used in aircraft without requiring them to be blended with conventional fuel, according to the Defense Innovation Unit. Air Company’s process uses carbon dioxide and hydrogen to manufacture fuel, with the goal of reducing dependence on transported fuel supplies. The $65 million figure is a contract ceiling, not a guarantee that the government will pay the full amount. It represents the maximum value announced for the contract rather than confirmation of money already disbursed or fuel already delivered at commercial scale.AIRCO’s later announcements cite a $67 million contract and approximately $70 million in government workOn March 10, 2026, AIRCO announced development of its MAD Fuel System, a containerised platform intended to produce synthetic fuels at or near the point of use. The company expands MAD as “Mobile, Adaptable and Dynamic.” The system is designed to combine carbon dioxide, hydrogen and an energy source to produce fully formulated synthetic fuels, including aviation fuel. A containerised system could, in principle, be transported to remote sites instead of requiring fuel to be shipped over long distances. The announcement describes a technology under development, rather than a completed network of operational fuel-production units.AIRCO’s March 2026 announcement cited a $67 million Defense Innovation Unit contract through Project SynCE. The same announcement described approximately $70 million in work involving multiple US government offices, including a new $15 million Strategic Funding Increase award from AFWERX, the US Air Force’s innovation organisation. The public figures do not clearly explain how the $65 million ceiling announced in 2023 relates to the later $67 million figure, or precisely how the approximately $70 million total is calculated. They should therefore be reported separately rather than added together or presented as a reconciled funding total. The company has also identified airline partners, including JetBlue and Virgin Atlantic, in its public materials. Such partnerships indicate commercial interest, but they should not be interpreted as proof that those airlines are already purchasing synthetic fuel from AIRCO at commercial scale.The challenge is scaling synthetic fuel productionAIRCO’s work illustrates the difference between demonstrating a chemical process and producing enough fuel to serve a large industrial customer. The company’s consumer products showed that its carbon-conversion technology could be used to make saleable goods. The defence project, by contrast, requires a system capable of producing usable fuel reliably in environments where energy, equipment and logistics may be constrained. The environmental case also depends on how the fuel is produced. Synthetic fuel made from carbon dioxide can potentially reduce reliance on fossil-derived feedstocks, but its lifecycle emissions depend on the energy and hydrogen used in production. Carbon dioxide captured from one source and later released when fuel is burned does not, by itself, establish that the entire process removes more carbon than it emits.You use AI every day. articles.title: Facts are hares, but truth is a tortoise
articles.summary: Don’t believe every ‘study’ that comes your way Last year, researchers at King’s College London reported that theobromine, a key component of cocoa, might
articles.body: Don’t believe every ‘study’ that comes your wayLast year, researchers at King’s College London reported that theobromine, a key component of cocoa, might have anti-ageing properties. In July this year, sports scientists at University of Malaya, Kuala Lumpur, said merely sniffing chocolate before a workout could help you do more reps. Might, could – nothing definite there, yet we lap up such “research”.It doesn’t matter when all you’re doing is nibbling on a harmless piece of chocolate, but what if the research or advice happens to be medical? Did you get a scare when Trump’s FDA last year said taking paracetamol while pregnant could increase your child’s risk of autism?We are drowning in research today, journalist Helen Pearson writes in her book Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works. In 2025 alone, some 7mn scholarly articles were published worldwide – over 19,000 a day, Pearson says. There could be hundreds of papers on the same subject, with differing conclusions. For example, some research shows an occasional glass of wine is good for you, while others deem even a drop of alcohol harmful. How do we arrive at the truth?The old and easy way was to count the research. If four papers said wine is unhealthy and five said it isn’t, you could read it as a licence to drink. But this was problematic. What if the five pro reports had sampled only five subjects, whereas the four anti reports had sampled 5,000? And often, even this “vote counting” wasn’t considered necessary.Pearson mentions a mistake in the most popular baby and child care book of all time that might have resulted in up to 50,000 deaths in US, Europe and Australasia. In the 1957 edition of the guide, she says, its author, Dr Benjamin Spock, changed his advice on putting babies to bed.They ought to sleep face down, rather than on their backs, he wrote. Why? Because another famous doctor, Paul Woolley Jr, had said so in a study published in 1945. What followed was a spate of sudden infant death syndrome or Sids. It wasn’t until 1991, after doing “studies of studies”, that govts strongly advised making babies sleep on their backs.Those studies of studies, or systematic reviews, Pearson says, are the basis of what we now call evidence-based medicine. They come in various forms – meta-analyses, living reviews (where the conclusion can change with emerging evidence), etc – and, surprise, they are only 35 years old.They’ve become so important that in 2019, there were 29,000 systematic reviews in the field of medicine alone. Thanks to them, we know that there’s no “clear link” between maternal paracetamol use during pregnancy and autism or ADHD in offspring.Systematic reviews are the ultimate test of any claim, be it in medicine or environmental science, or even management theory. For example, they show that “a lot of standard management practices – like performance appraisals – are not supported by strong evidence showing they help”.So, how do flimsy, unproven theories – like chocolate’s anti-ageing effect – go viral? It’s because systematic reviews take three years, on average. They’re costly too, and AI isn’t much help yet, because it can hallucinate and lead us to the wrong conclusions. So myths and fads continue flying. What are you reading this with, protein coffee or a turmeric-ginger shot?You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's 'veg-only kitchen' diktat on first day of assuming office sparks row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only has sparked a political controversy, with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only has sparked a political controversy, with Congress leader K C Venugopal accusing him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda.Mathur, the former Sikkim governor, directed that non-vegetarian food should not be prepared or served in the Lok Bhavan kitchen. The reports surfaced on Thursday, a day before he assumed office, news agency PTI reported.Reacting to the reports shortly after Mathur was sworn in as the 29th governor of Keralam, AICC general secretary Venugopal alleged that the decision went beyond the governor's personal food preferences and infringed on individual freedom.Keralam has a diverse food culture and abundant fish resources as a coastal state, Venugopal said, adding that people had the freedom to choose between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food."Any attempt to restrict the food habits Keralites are accustomed to or dictate what they should eat from now on cannot be accepted," he said as quoted by PTI.Venugopal argued that restrictions that "intrude" into people's food choices and seek to erase Keralam's traditional way of life violate fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.He alleged that the governor was using his authority to "curtail" individual freedom instead of protecting people's right to decide what to eat and how to live."This is a continuation of the unconstitutional interests of the Sangh Parivar. This is the first step towards implementing the saffron agenda of the Sangh Parivar in Keralam," the Alappuzha MP alleged.While acknowledging Mathur's right to follow a vegetarian diet, Venugopal said the governor should not impose his personal preferences on the Lok Bhavan kitchen, whose employees include Keralites. He urged Mathur to withdraw any decision restricting food choices.What Lok Bhavan sources saidSources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian and had directed that non-vegetarian food not be prepared in the kitchen where his meals were cooked.They clarified that the kitchen's food was served only to the governor and a few members of his personal staff. Other employees either brought food from home or ate outside, and no restrictions had been imposed on their food choices, the sources said as cited by PTI.They added that fish and meat dishes had been prepared in the Lok Bhavan kitchen during the tenure of some previous governors.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: With no approved vaccine for Ebola strain, WHO begins first clinical trial in DR Congo
articles.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has announced the launch of the first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine during the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic
articles.body: The World Health Organization (WHO) has announced the launch of the first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine during the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).WHO director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Friday that the first participants had received the Ervebo vaccine in Bunia, the capital of Ituri province in northeastern DRC, which is at the centre of the outbreak.The trial will assess whether Ervebo, which is approved for protection against the Zaire strain of Ebola, can provide any cross-protection against the Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current epidemic, according to news agency AP.“This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work,” Tedros said in a post on X.DR Congo reports thousands of Ebola casesThe DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May, which has become the country's worst on record. Since then, the outbreak has resulted in more than 9,700 reported cases and over 4,600 deaths.In response to the crisis, the WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern, its second-highest level of alert.The outbreak has also been reported in four countries across eastern, central and western Africa, marking the widest geographical spread of an Ebola outbreak on the continent so far.Multiple vaccine candidates to be assessedKnown as the Tumaini trial, the initiative follows a single clinical trial framework designed to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and immunogenicity of multiple vaccine candidates.The study will adopt a ring vaccination strategy, under which people identified as close contacts of infected individuals and considered at high risk of contracting the virus will be vaccinated.In addition to Ervebo, the trial is expected to include two experimental vaccines specifically developed against the Bundibugyo virus. Both candidates are currently progressing through smaller, early-stage clinical studies.One candidate is an adenoviral vector vaccine, ChAdOx1, being developed by the University of Oxford. The other is an mRNA-based vaccine developed by US biotechnology company Moderna.The coalition for epidemic preparedness innovations (CEPI) has funded both candidates and said they are expected to enter the trial shortly.The study will also include pregnant women and children aged 12 years and above, helping generate evidence for groups that are frequently excluded from clinical research.WHO stresses need for evidence on vaccine protectionWHO emergencies director Chikwe Ihekweazu said the trial had been designed to produce robust scientific evidence on whether the participating vaccines could protect people at risk of infection.The findings are expected to help researchers determine whether the existing vaccine and the experimental candidates can offer protection against the Bundibugyo strain, for which vaccine options remain limited.The trial represents an important step in efforts to evaluate potential vaccines amid the ongoing Ebola emergency in the DRC and other affected parts of Africa.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran has "increased efforts to target U.S. personnel," intel chief warns
articles.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned in a memo to Secretary of State Rubio that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. pers...
articles.body:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Friday that Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel" abroad, with plots to kill Americans reaching "advanced stages" in the Middle East and other countries.

The warning, contained in an unclassified memo that was sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and obtained by CBS News, comes as the State Department adjusts staffing at diplomatic posts across the Middle East , and the U.S. military pares back its footprint in the region, amid concerns about direct threats from Iran and threats from the Iranian-backed Houthi movement in Yemen.

"The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries," Clayton wrote.

The memo, which was issued as the Trump administration weighs resuming military strikes against Iran, does not identify specific targets or countries where the alleged plots are underway, or indicate whether attacks may be imminent.

Clayton said the U.S. intelligence community is working to downgrade sensitive intelligence — received through various channels — so it can be shared more broadly with State Department personnel. CIA Director John Ratcliffe was copied on the memo.

The warning follows a series of precautions at U.S. diplomatic facilities across the region. Earlier this week, the State Department ordered non-essential U.S. embassy personnel and their families to depart Saudi Arabia. Several other American embassies in the region adjusted their staffing under "restricted operations" status, which allows them to reduce the number of personnel without formally going on ordered departure, CBS News previously reported.

"When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment," a U.S. official told CBS News on Friday. "The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO [Restricted Operations] Status in the region."

A U.S. official and a senior U.S. military official also told CBS News this week that the military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing threats.

Houthi militants have stepped up drone and missile attacks against Saudi Arabia, targeting oil infrastructure and airports. One strike on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport earlier this month killed at least a dozen people , including a U.S. citizen, and injured hundreds more.

Last weekend, U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and other countries warned Americans to exercise caution due to Houthi attacks.

Although the U.S. and Iran have refrained from striking each other in recent weeks, President Trump has not ruled out restarting hostilities after next month's midterm elections. Iran has also continued to take responsibility for attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

At a campaign rally in Florida on Friday, Mr. Trump suggested the U.S. could launch another operation against Iran if Tehran failed to reach an agreement.

"We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree," the president said, invoking the name of the U.S. military campaign launched in February.
