articles.title: Inside England’s Alnwick Poison Garden, hundreds of dangerous plants grow behind locked gates, and visitors are warned not to touch, smell or taste them
articles.summary: Most gardens invite you to wander, sniff the roses and pick a flower. One of the most famous gardens in England does the exact opposite.
articles.body: Most gardens invite you to wander, sniff the roses and pick a flower. One of the most famous gardens in England does the exact opposite. Tucked away next to Alnwick Castle in Northumberland, the Poison Garden sits behind black iron gates that stay locked, and you can only go in with a guide. According to the Alnwick Garden’s own website, it’s filled with around 100 toxic, intoxicating and narcotic plants, and visitors are strictly forbidden from smelling, touching or tasting any of them. It’s a garden built to teach people that beauty and danger can grow side by side.A duchess with an unusual ideaThe garden was started in 2005 by Jane Percy, the Duchess of Northumberland, as part of the 12-acre Alnwick Garden on the grounds of her family’s estate, according to NPR. HGTV reports that she created it to help educate schoolchildren about the dangers of harmful and illicit drugs, which come from the sort of compounds these plants produce. In the Middle Ages and Renaissance, plants like these were used both as medicines and as poisons, so the garden also tells a long human story about how thin that line can be.Locked gates and a very strict ruleThe gates themselves set the tone. National Geographic describes the black iron gates as decorated with skulls, and the garden is packed with more than a hundred varieties of plants so deadly you can’t enter without supervision. As tours begin, guides warn visitors not to touch, lick or pick, and share stories of historic poisoners along with the plants they used. The unofficial motto is “look, don’t touch,” and head gardener Trevor Jones told NPR that visitors aren’t allowed to smell, touch or taste any plants.Caged plants and hazmat suitsSome plants are considered so dangerous that they live in cages. The Alnwick Garden’s website says the most hazardous ones are kept inside giant cages. Atlas Obscura adds that the garden is locked at night under a 24-hour security watch. Even the people who look after the plants take no chances, and National Geographic shows professional handlers working in masks, gloves and hazmat suits. For the rest of us, simply standing in the garden means keeping our hands to ourselves and staying close to the guide.The plants that make people faintSome of the plants don’t need to be touched to cause trouble. HGTV says black henbane gives off a strong smell that can be overwhelming on a warm day, and visitors often faint near it, which is why there’s a bench nearby and first aiders on standby. Angel’s trumpet, or Brugmansia, has fragrant blooms that disguise a potent hallucinogen. National Geographic reports that the keepers expect many fainters every year. The Alnwick Garden itself says some visitors still occasionally pass out from breathing in toxic fumes.Danger that grows closer to homeFor all its drama, the garden’s main message is surprisingly down to earth. National Geographic notes that visitors learn about the dangers of poisonous plants, including ones that grow in ordinary backyards. A castor plant grows in the garden, as NPR points out, and the plant is far more common than many people realise. Guides also run a foraging-themed tour on what not to pick in the wild. Leave with one lesson: unfamiliar plants deserve respect, and a pretty flower isn’t always a harmless one.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border management remains in focus
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju extended greetings to personnel of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) on the force's Raising Day on Saturday, praising their courage, sacrifices and service in protecting India's borders.The Indian Army also conveyed its wishes to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of the force's 65th Raising Day.In a post on X, Prime Minister Modi praised the force's personnel, known as Himveers, for their valour and determination in facing challenges.“On their Raising Day, greetings to all personnel of the ITBP. The ITBP Himveers have distinguished themselves through their exceptional valour. They have always risen to every challenge with remarkable determination. Their selfless service and sacrifices are a source of immense inspiration to the nation,” PM Modi wrote.Union home minister Amit Shah also extended Raising Day greetings to ITBP personnel, praising their courage in safeguarding the country's security and remembering those who laid down their lives in service to the nation.“The roar of their valour echoes through the snow-clad mountains, reducing every threat to our nation's security to rubble. Their tenacity in withstanding the harshest climates symbolizes India's steely resolve for security. Salutations to the martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation,” Shah wrote on X.Rajnath Singh, Kiren Rijiju salute ITBP personnelDefence minister Rajnath Singh extended his greetings to ITBP personnel and their families, highlighting their contribution to border security and internal security operations.“On ITBP Raising Day, I extend my warm greetings to all ITBP personnel and their families. The Himveers of ITBP have played a vital role in safeguarding India’s borders in the harshest climatic conditions. They have also made significant contributions to internal security operations, including efforts to combat Left Wing Extremism,” Singh said.He added that their courage, professionalism and commitment to duty reflected the finest traditions of service to the nation.Kiren Rijiju also greeted the Himveers, invoking the force's motto, “शौर्य-दृढ़ता-कर्मनिष्ठा” (valour, steadfastness and devotion to duty).“On the occasion of ITBP Raising Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to the Himveers of @ITBP_official. Your vital resilience in protecting our borders in extreme conditions is an inspiration. Salute to your spirit of sacrifices & patriotism,” Rijiju wrote on X.Indian Army extends wishes on ITBP's 65th Raising DayThe Indian Army also conveyed its greetings to the force. In a post on X, it said General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of Army Staff, and all ranks of the Army extended their “warm greetings and best wishes” to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of its 65th Raising Day.The ITBP is responsible for guarding India's borders with China in challenging high-altitude and climatic conditions.The greetings come amid continuing attention to the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday that the situation along the India-China border gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.“Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC),” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.Jaiswal also said the two countries had agreed to discuss ways to improve their understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to strengthen border management. He stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur had recently spoken about continuing confrontations with Chinese troops at several locations along the border in Arunachal Pradesh.He also said the force had raised drone platoons in all its border units and developed a new 'Strike' course to better handle battles similar to the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: Iran mocks Trump on busy Tehran street, shows US president taking nap behind bars
articles.summary: A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran, where he can be seen
articles.body: A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran, where he can be seen rattling the bars and taking a nap in a staged display targeting Washington over a deadly strike on an Iranian wedding.The installation, placed above Tajrish Square, one of Tehran's busiest transport hubs, features an actor wearing a Trump mask and wig inside a mock prison cell equipped with a bed, toilet and sink. The performance has drawn crowds, with passersby stopping to film the spectacle.An electronic billboard behind the cage displays images related to a US strike that hit a wedding in the southern Iranian town of Kuhestak last month. The display also features crime-scene imagery, linking the attack to its message against the US president.The installation was unveiled on Tuesday by Tehran's Beautification Organization, which is affiliated with the city's municipality, according to Iranian state media. It appears to be part of a 15-day campaign highlighting the wedding strike.The display comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February. Tehran has increasingly used public billboards to deliver political messages against Washington, including a previous display showing Trump lying in a graffiti-covered coffin.Iranian authorities and supporters have also circulated online memes and videos mocking Trump and his administration during the conflict.The wedding strike has become a focus of the latest campaign. US Central Command had said it was aware of Iranian reports about the incident and that American forces do not target civilians. A visual analysis by The New York Times, along with an assessment by a weapons expert, indicated that an American bomb struck the wedding as US forces carried out attacks in southern Iran.You use AI every day.
